# C1 rule: when is a printed direction of error change resolved?

Written before any recomputation in this pass. The rule follows an advisory proposal
of 19 November. That proposal already quoted the
N611, N497 and P25 (0.01 mesh) table values, so the rule is not blind to those three
contrasts. It is fixed before it is applied to every other printed direction and to
the full set of nine hill contrasts.

## Quantities

For one output, a baseline run value b, an alternative run value a and a reference r
give the change in absolute error

    D = |a - r| - |b - r|        (D < 0: alternative closer; D > 0: alternative farther)

## Admissible values

Each printed number x stands for the interval [x - h, x + h], where h is half a unit
in its last printed decimal place, read from the mechanically captured digit string
(`pdftotext -layout`), not from a transcription. Where the source gives an interval
for the reference (r +/- u, or a printed range r1-r2), the reference interval is
widened by it. A value read from a plotted curve carries the reading half-width
recorded with that reading; if none was recorded the value is "plot reading, no
half-width" and the output is unresolved unless the source itself states the direction.

## Resolution of one output (primary rule)

Evaluate D over the box of admissible (a, b, r). The direction is
- resolved closer   if max D < 0,
- resolved farther  if min D > 0,
- unresolved        otherwise.
The box extrema are found exactly (D is piecewise linear; evaluate at the box corners
and at a = r, b = r where those lie inside the box).

Reported next to the primary result, without changing the class: the proposal's
simpler threshold |D| > h_a + h_b + h_r + u_r, and the nominal D.

Where a source prints more than one reference for an output, each is evaluated
separately. The output is resolved only if every printed reference that the source
offers for that output gives the same resolved direction; otherwise it is
"reference dependent" and counts as unresolved. The reference the paper's own table
designates is named.

## Controls

Read from the source for the two runs: (i) nominal mesh including first-cell spacing,
(ii) outer subgrid or turbulence closure and numerical scheme, (iii) flow and forcing,
(iv) statistics accumulation window. Each is recorded as equal, different or not
reported. The changed wall treatment itself, including what it necessarily changes
(for example a first-cell eddy viscosity that is part of the treatment, or the
sampling height it prescribes), is the intervention and is recorded as such, not as a
control difference.

`controls_status` is "documented equal" only if all four are stated equal,
"differ" if any is stated different, otherwise "not all reported".

## Class of a two-output contrast (exactly one)

Applied in this order:
1. unrankable: an error is undefined for a run (for example no separation bubble).
2. unresolved: at least one of the two directions is unresolved or reference dependent.
3. controls differ: both directions resolved, but `controls_status` is "differ".
4. resolved opposing: both resolved, opposite signs.
5. resolved concordant: both resolved, same sign.

Classes 4 and 5 carry the flag "averaging window not reported" (or the other missing
control) where `controls_status` is "not all reported". Counts are given both for all
class-4/5 contrasts and for the subset with documented equal controls.

A single-output direction statement uses: unrankable / unresolved / controls differ /
resolved closer / resolved farther, with the same flags.

## What the rule does not cover

It bounds rounding and reported reference intervals only. Sampling error, discretisation
error and experimental uncertainty enter only where the source reports them. A resolved
class therefore means "resolved to the printed precision and reported intervals".
Magnitudes are reported with every class so that a small resolved change is visible.

## Scope of application

Every sentence of the manuscript (abstract, Sections 1-5, captions, tables) that states
that one calculation is closer to or farther from a reference than another for a named
output, or that an error rose or fell. Statements that only repeat a source's own
qualitative verdict without numbers are listed with class "source-stated, no number
extracted" and are not counted as resolved by this rule.

## Bump station x/L = -0.4 (P31)

The rule written at 00:43 (paired_p_work/bump_rule.txt) stays primary: mean absolute
velocity discrepancy over the full shared support. Added in this pass, as description
and not as a second ranking rule: the ranking as a function of the lower bound of the
support, the two crossover heights (cumulative-support and pointwise) in units of y/L
and of fine-mesh cells, the signed mean discrepancy below and above the crossover, and
any stated uncertainty of the PIV reference if a lawfully accessible source gives one.
The manuscript sentence on a restricted height range may state only what these give.
